title: slider-svg-2d widget params
description: Shared chrome renderer for the standard 'slider(s) + SVG + readout' interactive widget pattern. Pulls the slider config, SVG sizing, and readout id out of the previously-opaque verbatim bodyMarkup into typed params. The driving script stays as a `script` param (each widget's draw logic is genuinely bespoke), but the chrome HTML is generated deterministically from `controls` + `svg` + `readout`. First batch of the verbatim-slug hoisting effort (PLAN.md 'Hoist semantic params out of verbatim slugs').

widgetId.description: DOM id label for the widget. Two semantically distinct uses across the corpus, distinguished by `wrapperHasId`: (1) when `wrapperHasId` is false or omitted, widgetId is metadata-only — used by widget-script `ref` binding (see render-doc.mjs::buildWidgetById) to attach a trailing `<script>` block to its widget. The wrapper carries no id (spectral-theory style). (2) when `wrapperHasId` is true, widgetId IS the wrapper's `id` attribute, emitted as `<div class="widget" id="{widgetId}">` (kahler-geometry style). New widgets typically omit; preserve verbatim through migration so byte-identical roundtrip holds.

wrapperHasId.description: When true, emit `widgetId` as the wrapper div's `id` attribute. When false or omitted, keep the canonical slim wrapper `<div class="widget">` (widgetId is then metadata-only — used by widget-script ref-binding). See `widgetId` description for the two corpus styles.

title.description: Header title shown in .hd > .ttl and also placed inside the SVG's <title> element. May contain KaTeX $...$.

hint.description: Header hint shown in .hd > .hint. May contain KaTeX $...$.

controls.description: Ordered controls inside the .row above the SVG. Renders one element per item in source order. Must be non-empty (the renderer throws on empty — this constraint surfaces the rule at validate time instead). Most widgets have 1-3 sliders plus an optional status span; some add a toggle button.

oneOf.$comment: Slider control. min<max and value∈[min,max] are enforced by the renderer (renderControl asserts both), but JSON Schema 2020-12 can't cross-reference sibling properties without an `if/then` per slider — too noisy. The pre-save migration script's byte-identity guard catches any inconsistency that would otherwise slip past.

label.description: Label text wrapping or preceding the input (form-dependent — see `format`). May contain KaTeX $...$ and inline HTML (e.g. a trailing `<span>` for slider-value display).

step.description: Optional; omitted from the rendered <input> when absent (browser default = 1). Number OR string — strings preserve a trailing `.0` suffix from the source HTML when present (so `"1.0"` renders as `step="1.0"`, not `step="1"`).

value.description: Initial value (the `value` attribute on <input>). Number OR string — strings preserve decimal formatting from the source HTML (`"3.0"` vs `"3"`).

format.description: Markup shape. `nested` (default) emits `<label>{label}<input id="{id}" type="range" …></label>` — input is a child of label. `separate` emits `<label for="{id}">{label}</label>` followed by a sibling `<input type="range" id="{id}" …>`. Corpus split: spectral-theory uses nested; kahler-geometry / spectral-methods-data / mathematical-biology use separate. Preserved per-control so byte-identity holds across the variations.

labelAttrs.description: Optional verbatim attribute string spliced into the `<label …>` opening tag (e.g. ` style="margin-left:1rem"`). Includes the leading space. Preserved verbatim so corpus-specific cosmetic CSS survives migration. Most widgets omit this.

class.description: Optional CSS class on the button (e.g. `active` for a toggle-button group's pre-selected state). Omitted from the rendered `<button>` when absent.
CSS class for the span. Omit to emit a `<span>` with no class attribute (kahler-geometry style); set to `"small"` for the spectral-theory style.

text.description: Initial inner text; usually empty since the driving script fills it on first draw.

viewBox.description: SVG viewBox `min-x min-y width height` — origin coordinates may be negative, but width and height must be positive (zero-sized SVG would be invisible).

width.description: Optional. Positive number (px) or a percent string like "100%". Legacy widgets pin an explicit size; modern responsive widgets omit width/height entirely and size from viewBox + CSS max-width:100%. When omitted, the renderer leaves the attribute off.

height.description: Optional. Positive number (px) or a percent string like "100%". Omit alongside width for a responsive viewBox-only SVG.

role.description: Optional ARIA role for the SVG (corpus convention is `img` when set, paired with aria-label). Round-tripped from pages that set it; omitted otherwise.

ariaLabel.description: Optional `aria-label` accessibility name on the SVG element itself (distinct from the `<title>` child). Round-tripped from pages that set it. HTML-escaped by the renderer.

title.description: Optional override for the SVG's `<title>` accessibility name. When omitted, the renderer uses the header `title` field (the canonical convention — every spectral-theory widget matches). Many corpus widgets give the SVG a more specific accessibility label than the page header (e.g. header `$(p,q)$-bigrading explorer` vs SVG title `bidegree summands`); preserve that distinction through migration. HTML-escaped by the renderer.

oneOf.description:
true: emit `
`; false: omit the readout div.

class.description: CSS class on the readout div. Default 'readout' matches the verbatim convention.

oneOf.description: Use when the readout id doesn't follow the `{svg-prefix}-readout` convention (e.g. when the SVG id is `kernel-svg` but the readout id is `kernel-readout` and you want explicit pairing).

bodyScript.description: Verbatim driving `<script>(function(){ ... })();</script>` block. Each widget's draw logic is genuinely bespoke (axes, bars, level lines, curve sampling, …); only the chrome is shared. Named bodyScript (rather than `script`) so the XSS-lint passthrough in validate-widget-params.mjs covers it — the lint refuses to accept `<script>` inside ANY other param key.

trailingProse.description:
Optional `

...

` prose block emitted between the readout div and the wrapper's closing ``. Some corpus widgets (spectral-methods-data, etc.) embed an explanatory caption inside the widget — this preserves it through migration. The renderer emits the prose verbatim wrapped in `

…

` with the appropriate indentation. Most widgets omit this field.

$comment: When `readout: true`, the renderer derives the readout div's id by stripping the `-svg` suffix from `svg.id`. This conditional clause enforces the suffix invariant in AJV instead of letting it throw at render time.
